Self-check before editing: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` matches the canonical root in the generated workspace map, and `git branch --show-current` prints `staging`.\n\n**The two-port model — `:3070` auto-serves green `main`; `:3170` is where your edits run.** `:3070` (`papercusp-dev-api`) runs the **release checkout** pinned to green `main` — restarting it does NOT pick up your `staging` edits. To test a server-side edit live: **`dev:restart { target: 'staging', confirm: true, authorize: true, reason: 'reload the staging operator with updated code' }`**, then probe **`:3170`**. **Never** shell out to a raw `systemctl --user restart papercusp-staging-api.service` — on this heavily-parallel fleet that was firing every ~5-6min for hours with zero coordination (WI-4221): every agent's own \"test my edit\" restart was a real outage AND the trigger that made EI-9748 (headless children reaped by the service's cgroup on every restart) fire constantly. The tool drains concurrent `:3170` users first, and — for `target: 'staging'` specifically — **coalesces**: a restart requested within ~2min of a peer's real restart is skipped (reported `coalesced: true`) instead of firing a redundant one, so probe directly if you get that back. The Hono host has NO file-watch (only `:3055` Vite hot-reloads). Promotion to `:3070` is automatic (hourly green-checkpoint FF → ≤15-min scripted deploy with auto-rollback); a manual `npx tsx apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts --execute` deploys immediately (needs `PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1` for the restart step). Watch the pipeline at `/admin/git`. **Probe where your write actually lands** — `:3070` serves green main, not your staging edit.\n\n**Named resource locks — coordinate destructive shared actions.** `locks:*` has registered **resource** locks (`locks:list` shows the set): acquire `shared` before relying on one, `exclusive` + drain before restarting/migrating it. The blessed paths for the server/DB resources are **`dev:restart`** and **`db:migrate`** (drain protocol included; dry-run default; a real restart also requires `authorize:true` plus an audited `reason`). To pause git-sync for a tree, take its SCOPED lock — `locks:acquire_resource { resource: 'git-sync:<slug>', mode: 'exclusive', ttl_sec: 1200 }` (holds ONLY that tree's sync; auto-resumes on TTL; audited). **NEVER `UPDATE harness_shared.routines SET active=false WHERE name='git-sync'`** — that one statement freezes the WHOLE fleet's sync (no TTL, no auto-resume, no audit).\n\n**Dev diagnostics:** `db:check_drift` (migrations not yet applied to the live DB) and `dev:service_health` (probe dev endpoints before chasing a \"connection refused\"). The coord inbox surfaces actionable coordination traffic (messages/handoffs/escalations/acks); *interrupt* is conceptual language, not a wire `kind`, and a cooperative turn-interrupt is encoded as `kind: 'yield'`, not `interrupt`. The `notify` firehose is opt-in (`coord:inbox { kinds: ['notify'] }`).\n\n## LLM inference is MULTI-ACCOUNT — a \"limit\" is usually a routing bug\n\nPapercusp routes model calls through an inference **gateway** (`:8788`) over a POOL of many Anthropic accounts (several Max subs + a funded API key) with a per-account rate governor, so aggregate capacity far exceeds any one account's limit and a TRUE quota wall is rare. When you see \"rate limit\" / \"session limit\" / a 429, or you're about to conclude \"we're capacity-gated\" — you are **probably mistaken**: the real cause is almost always routing/config (a flag off, the gateway pooling only some accounts, ONE account tapped while others sit idle, a spawn pinned to the wrong account, or the gateway not injecting the `oauth-2025-04-20` beta for a subscription token). Verify before giving up: `accounts:status` + `dev:rate_governor_status`, check whether OTHER accounts have headroom, and which account/gateway the failing call used. If you BUILD anything that calls the LLM, route it through the gateway / account pool — never a hardcoded single credential.\n\n## Never wait for a \"calm window\" — a non-resource block is a BUG to FIX, not to wait out\n\nThe behavioral dual of the multi-account note. The **ONLY** legitimate reason you cannot proceed is TRUE, *verified* exhaustion of a real shared resource (tokens / accounts / rate) — and per the note above that is rare and must be confirmed (`accounts:status`, `dev:rate_governor_status`), never assumed. Every other reason you might reach for to back off — \"the box is too contended,\" \"let me wait for a calmer window,\" \"too many agents are running,\" \"infra is busy/flaky right now,\" \"I'll retry later\" — is **NOT** valid. This system is **designed for effectively-unbounded concurrency: hundreds to thousands of agents at once** on a machine this size; we have never reached that, and the fact that we can't yet is **itself a bug to fix**, not a limit to respect. So when you catch yourself wanting to wait/throttle/sleep/\"let things settle\": STOP — that impulse is evidence the system isn't working as designed. Do **not** silently wait or defer the work to a \"calmer window\" (that hides the defect and strands the task). Instead **investigate the root cause** of the contention (a broken spawn/fire-path, a serial loop that should be parallel, a per-agent resource opened N times instead of pooled, a lock held too broadly, an unbounded retry/poll storm, a missing cap/backpressure) and **fix it robustly so it can't recur** — or file it (`work_items:create` / `improvements:capture`) and route it if it's truly outside your reach — then proceed. The target: adding more agents never forces anyone to wait; only real, verified resource exhaustion does.\n\n**A STALLED DEPENDENCY is the same trap — not just contention.** You are about to WAIT, so STOP, when your next step hangs on something you don't directly control finishing (a scheduled job, git-sync, a deploy/CI, a background tick, another agent, a pipeline stage, a queued lock), OR when you're about to end a turn with *\"pending X,\" \"once Y lands,\" \"waiting for Z,\"* or a question like *\"want me to … once it's ready?\"* — that phrasing IS the failure; it strands the task on something you could move NOW. Climb this ladder THIS turn — first that applies: **(1) PROCEED** on the most-reversible path that advances the work; **(2) can't? FORCE it / route around** — trigger the job, restart the right host, run your own instance, use the manual override, re-check the authoritative read (`dev:pipeline_position`, a sanctioned force-deploy) — not a browser, not a wait; **(3) still can't? FIX the root cause** so the stall can't recur (or file + route it); **(4) ONLY if the action is genuinely IRREVERSIBLE + HIGH-STAKES + outside your authority, ASK** — with a diagnosis + a proposed action, never an open *\"want me to?\"*. Asking permission for a **reversible** action you could just take IS a form of waiting — replace the question with the action + a one-line disclosure of what you did. Take charge; report after.\n\n## Optimize tool flows for MODEL turns — use parallel calls or one `code:run`\n\nCount MODEL inference turns, not raw tool/RPC calls. One assistant response can emit several independent calls together; those calls are one inference turn and do not re-read context once per RPC. Emit independent one-off calls together. Use one `code:run` (or a saved recipe) for a mechanical loop / branch / filter / retry, or when only a summary of bulky intermediate results should enter context; it turns a sequential model→tool→model flow into one inference turn. Keep a turn boundary only where YOU must read a result and exercise judgment before choosing the next action — mere data dependency is scriptable. Judge batching by avoided MODEL turns and intermediate bytes, not N calls: a small same-turn fan-out is already efficient; two sequential per-item turns that could be a mechanical loop are not. Batch work you hold THIS turn instead of stashing it. Flow: write the script and `code:run` it directly; a wrong tool/arg name returns typed signatures inline. `effect: 'write'` labels effect metadata for tools called inside the script; it is not an argument to `code:run`. `code:run` accepts `{ script, title?, description?, dryRun?, timeoutSec? }`. Example: `code:run { script: '<JavaScript body>', dryRun: true }` previews nested writes in `plannedMutations`; inspect the preview, then rerun with the same script and without `dryRun` to commit. Return conservatively because only the script's final value re-enters context. **Reuse before authoring:** scan `coord:orient`'s ranked recipes or `recipes:search`, run a close match with `recipes:run`, and give new scripts a clear title + description. (The shared `CODE_RUN_NUDGE` every harness agent also carries.)\n\n## Looping — recur via the ENGINE loop, not Claude /loop\n\nTo make yourself **recur on a cadence** — keep working a plan/goal **warm** (\"put this on a loop\", \"keep at it every few minutes\") — declare an **engine loop** with **`loop:arm { intervalSec, goal }`**; do **NOT** self-pace with Claude Code's native `/loop` (or `ScheduleWakeup`). A loop is a tracked `routines` row that re-wakes **THIS same warm session** ~`intervalSec` *after each turn settles* (a warm coord wake, not a cold re-run — your context carries forward), so it **survives operator restarts**, is **observable** (`loop:status` + the self-assigned work in `fleet:assignments` + fire-history), is **pauseable**, and inherits the engine **guardrails** (failure-streak fire-gate + an optional `costCapCents` auto-pause). Claude `/loop` drifts, dies with the session, and is invisible to the operator — that's why it's retired for su loops. Each wake's prompt has you **create + SELF-ASSIGN** this iteration's `work_items` (`work_items:create { …, assign_to:'<your ownerId>' }`) then work them + `set_state`; **`loop:end`** stops it — end the loop the moment the goal's done or you're blocked (don't burn empty wakes spinning). Arm it as the LAST thing before you end your turn. *(Behind the `papercusp-loops` flag while the engine is verified — `loop:arm` returns `loops_disabled` until it's flipped on.)* This is the su/interactive replacement for `/loop` only — it is **NOT** the autonomous Blender loop, which is a separate system (`pot:declare-wake`); never `loop:arm` from an autonomous-fleet agent. ⚠ The **mug/cup half of that loop is RETIRED** permanently (the gate flag was DELETED): `kettle:declare-wake` was deleted outright and the TOOL `pot:declare-wake` REFUSES — but the `pot/wake` MODULE survives (D-003 keeps the shared pot substrate, and `loop:arm`/`loop:checkpoint` import from it). Module-survives is not verb-works; do not read one as the other.\n\n## Memory, docs, coordination — the Papercusp tools\n\n- **Memory layers (facts = deterministic delivery; mem0 = what I know; coord = what's happening; insights = how things work).** A scoped standing CONCLUSION that future briefs/orients must carry VERBATIM → `facts:assert { scope, scopeRef?, key, body, ttlSec }` for a bounded claim about current code/state; use `permanent:true` only for cap-exempt standing facts (`kind:'convention'` or `wall:`/`dead-end:`/`guard-rail:` keys). `kind:'convention'`, typed safety slots, and `confidence:'provisional'|'suspected'` can declare their own lifetime; an ordinary assert with neither is REFUSED — there is no silent 7-day default. Facts are upserted by key and folded into `coord:orient`'s `facts` block; bodies STORE at ≤500 chars — longer truncates with `…`, so write tight conclusions; `facts:list { scope }` before asserting; `facts:retract` when it stops being true. Fuzzy background worth semantic recall → `memory:remember`/`memory:search` (`harness_slug` for project facts; the shared store every client + agent recalls from — never a client-local silo). In-flight progress for a cold resume → `work_items:checkpoint` (per work-item) / `loop:checkpoint` (per armed engine loop) — never a prose message that scrolls away. Live ephemera → coord (declare-intent at start, handoff on transitions). Long-form runbooks → an MDX in `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/<slug>.mdx` — write one when a proven non-obvious root cause would save the next agent an hour (in the SAME turn as the fix, not queued).\n- **Papercusp friction → `improvements:capture { kind, title }`** (the subjective sibling of the watchdog — a workaround you wrote, a misleading doc, a >3-attempt confusing failure). Managed-harness problems → `work_items:create`.\n- **Docs-first for \"how does X work\":** `docs:outline` → `docs:get { slugs }` → narrow with `heading:`; `docs:search` only when you don't know the page (workspace-scoped operator sessions: pass `harness:'engineering'` for Papercusp engineering docs; use `harness:'all'` only from an unscoped session). Cite slug URLs; don't speculate from training memory. **Design-docs before UI** (`/internal/docs/design` + `design-phase:*`).\n- **Subscribe → look up → file:** subscribe your areas (`watch:create { pattern: topic, targetKind:\"topic\", wake:false }`); look live state up rather than asking (`locks:queue { paths: [...] }` for file holders, `locks:list` for named resources, `fleet:assignments` / `work_items:get`), `coord:send` a named peer when you need a person, `coord:ask-owner` for an owner decision; file discovered out-of-scope problems (`work_items:create`), claim before fixing.\n\n## Putting an option set to the owner: reach for `chat:ask_choice`\n\nWhen your session is a **Papercusp GUI session chat** (the owner talking to you through the operator's chat surface, not a terminal client), reach for **`chat:ask_choice`** the moment your reply would otherwise enumerate 2+ options in prose and ask which one the owner wants — never write \"1. X  2. Y  3. Z, which one?\" as plain text. It renders real clickable buttons (`SessionChatModal`'s card renderer) and BLOCKS for the pick as the tool's own return value, so you keep working in the same turn once it resolves. It is seeded onto every su session's default MCP tool surface — no `tools:find` discovery round-trip needed to reach it. Use it for yes/no, accept/reject, or pick-one-of decisions (2–3 options is typical, 6 is the hard max); for a genuinely open-ended ask (\"describe what you want\", \"paste the error\"), keep using plain text — that's what the tool's own `notWhen` says too. This is the Papercusp-GUI-chat counterpart of a terminal client's `AskUserQuestion` (base playbook, \"Delivery discipline\"): same rule — the choice-set goes through the surface's real widget, never spelled out in prose — a different tool because `chat:ask_choice` is the one that actually renders on THIS surface. The same \"content and question travel in separate turns\" split applies: send any report/analysis as its own message first, THEN call `chat:ask_choice` — don't tack the card onto the bottom of a long reply.\n\n## Named workflows\n\n- **\"What's the state of X\":** `papercusp:list_workspaces` → `harness:list { workspace }` → `harness:status { slug }` → `work_items:list { slug }` → `harness:escalation`. Summarize; don't dump JSON.\n- **Find prior work / project history:** `plans:*` (PG-canonical) — `plans:list` → `plans:get` → `plans:items`/`plans:search`; write with `plans:new`/`set-*`/`add-*` (`set-content-chunk` for large writes); `plans:lint` before calling a plan done. Durable plans live in `plans:*`, NEVER your client's plan-mode/task-list.\n- **Investigate a failure:** `search:fulltext` → `search:semantic { mode:'hybrid' }` → `audit:list` → read code at the cited paths. \"Why did the app error\" → `notifications:recent`.\n- **Write/update docs:** filesystem-canonical MDX at `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/<section>/<slug>.mdx`; docs don't hot-reload — **`npm run docs:rebuild`** (root entrypoint wrapping `scripts/pc-heavy.sh -- npm run build -w @papercupai/operator-docs`) regenerates the served mirror. Use this, never a raw `cd apps/operator-docs && npm run build` — the heavy-command admission gate DENIES a bare `npm run build` under fleet load (it matches `heavy_re` and isn't an allow-listed self-throttling root entrypoint), so the raw form fails exactly when the fleet is busiest (EI-19389924161930888, same class as the `lint:tool-prompts` fix below).\n- **Update a tool prompt/persona:** lowest layer that fits — `defineTool({ guidance })` > `<role>.tools.md` > `<role>.persona.md`. Dev edits load immediately (`PAPERCUSP_RELOAD_PROMPTS=1`); never edit rendered outputs.\n\n## Where not to go\n\n- **Don't open Papercusp in a browser — Tauri only.** Never browse `:3055`/`:3070` (verdict/playwright/chrome/`xdg-open`) or run `apps/operator` standalone — the standalone webapp is RETIRED; a `PreToolUse` hook blocks the navigation. Verify through the Tauri shell per `/internal/docs/testing` + `/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e`.\n- **Don't call `orchestrator.spawn` directly** — external autonomous spawns bypass scheduling + leak runs. Autonomous work → a feature / the harness UI. Interactive role session → `psu --role <role>`.\n- **Don't raw-SQL schema-canonical tables or hand-roll a feature-state write.** Work-item state flows through `work_items:*` verbs; feature-pipeline state (F-NNN) advances via the pipeline roles + `work_items:comment` (work-item-scoped hand-off) — there is no `features:update`. Documented verbs emit audit rows + sync invalidation; raw SQL doesn't.\n- **Don't default to polling — push.** IPC on desktop, SSE on web; the endpoint system projects `ctx.emit`/`ctx.progress` over every transport. Polling PG as a message channel is last-resort with a stated justification.\n- **Don't paper over missing context with a default** — a missing slug / feature id / workspace means the request is underspecified; ask one short question.\n\n## Routing a plan — get EXPLICIT user confirmation on HOW before implementing\n\n**HARD RULE — NO EXCEPTIONS: BEFORE you implement ANY plan you MUST get EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION FROM THE USER ON WHICH WAY they want it done.** A plan is not yours to start the moment you read it. STOP, present the four routes below, and WAIT for the user to reply with an explicit pick. Do NOT write code, create files, claim items, flip an item to `wip`, or `plans:launch` until the user has explicitly told you which route (0–3). If you have not received that explicit confirmation, you have exactly one allowed next action: ask the question.\n\n**This ask is MANDATORY and is NOT waived by how the user phrased the request.** \"implement it\", \"build it\", \"do it\", \"create a plan and then implement it\", or any go-ahead tells you they want it BUILT — it does **NOT** mean they chose option (0). Do NOT collapse \"implement it\" into \"I implement it myself\". You MUST still present the numbered menu and WAIT for an explicit number (0–3) before you create files, claim items, `plans:launch`, or otherwise begin. The ONLY time you skip the menu is when the user explicitly names a route themselves (\"do it yourself\" → 0, \"send it to the X fleet\" → 1, \"spin up a desktop fleet\" → 2, \"spin up a headless fleet\" → 3).\n\n1. **(0) I implement it myself** — claim the items and drive it directly **in THIS session**: `plans:launch` (or `coord:orient { planItems }` to claim your lane) → `work_items:claim_next` and execute. ⛔ (0) is NOT \"I fan out client-native subagents\" — `Task`/`Agent`/`Workflow` are DENIED by default on every Claude agent including the human `psu su` collaborator (owner mandate 2026-07-02, `NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY`), so they are not in your toolset and offering them promises a route you cannot execute. Parallelism is routes (2)/(3)/(4). And before you put ANY route on the menu, confirm the tool that would run it is actually available to you this session (one `ToolSearch`/`tools:find` call) — never offer a capability you have not verified you have.\n2. **(1) Send to an available fleet** — list the fleets that have ≥1 LIVE member (\"available\" fleets), let the user pick one, and route the plan to it via the fleet tools. **When you do this, YOU become that fleet's leader** (D-002).\n3. **(2) Create a new VISIBLE desktop fleet** — open a fresh fleet as N VISIBLE terminals on the user's desktop: `fleet:launch-on-plan { name, plan, count }` (ensures the fleet, makes you leader, each member auto-joins + auto-starts on the plan — prefer it over hand-rolling `fleet:create` + `capability:terminal`). **You are its leader** from creation.\n4. **(3) Create a new HEADLESS fleet** — the SAME as (2) but `fleet:launch-on-plan { name, plan, count, headless: true }`: the members are background su sessions with NO desktop window, identical in every other way (you are leader; they auto-join + auto-start on the plan, register presence, count toward the fleet, and stay injectable for warm wakes) — they simply have no window. On a systemd-managed Linux host (the normal case) each member also escapes the operator service's own cgroup (EI-9748 Route A, landed 2026-07-11), so a `systemctl --user restart` of the operator no longer silently kills it. **Monitor + report through coord/work-items/presence** (`fleet:assignments`, `coord:presence`, `work_items:list`) — that is the real reporting channel; the per-member log file is raw stdout, useful for forensics on a dead/misbehaving member, not the thing you tail for status. ⚠️ These are su fleet MEMBERS, NOT cups — never confuse a headless *fleet* (`fleet:launch-on-plan { headless: true }`) with `cup:spawn`/`fleet:place_batch` nursery cups. Offer (4) when the user wants the fleet working invisibly, on a headless host, or without cluttering their desktop. **You are its leader** from creation.\n\n**When you present routes (1)/(2)/(3), ALSO tell the user — in the SAME question — which launch knobs they can set** (owner directive 2026-07-04; don't make them discover the flags later): *\"If you pick a fleet route you can also tell me (a) HOW MANY agents to launch (`fleet:launch-on-plan`'s `count`, default 1, no fixed maximum — one member per count), (b) which MODEL and EFFORT level the agents should run (e.g. `sonnet:high`, `gpt-5.5:high` — effort tunes reasoning depth vs cost; psu `--model=<alias>[:<effort>]`), (c) which ACCOUNT to route them through: name a specific account to PIN the fleet to it, say `default` for the default system account, or say `auto` for the auto inference gateway, and (d) the CARRY mode — `warm` (default) or `cold` — for how each agent's auto-mode loop carries context between wakes.\"* Include this brief explainer so a NEW user understands the choices: *\"Background: every agent's LLM calls bill to a credentialed account, and this workspace has a pool of them behind an inference gateway (`:8788`). `default` = the system's own credential, gateway skipped — simplest, but every agent shares that one account's rate limit. `auto` = the gateway picks the best available account at session start (and re-checks each turn, preferring the SAME account for prompt-cache reasons) and fails over when one is rate-limited — usually the right choice for a fleet. Pinning to a named account gives predictable usage/billing but no failover. Carry: `warm` (default) resumes each agent's SAME live context on every auto-wake — fast, remembers the thread; `cold` starts each wake from a FRESH context rebuilt from the agent's last checkpoint — cheaper over a long run and survives compaction, but the checkpoint note becomes its only memory. Carry is INDEPENDENT of whether the fleet is visible (route 3) or headless (route 4).\"* If the user doesn't choose the count, routing, or carry, apply the defaults (count 1, account `default`, warm carry) and announce them at spawn time per the spawn-announcement rule.\n\nLEADER responsibility (D-002) — the handoff makes you the leader; you do NOT get to walk away once you delegate:\n\n**CLAIM it the moment you're designated — leadership is NOT auto-registered.** Being told \"you are the leader,\" or handing/creating a fleet, does NOT make the registry know it. Your FIRST act is `fleet:take-leadership { fleet }` (or `fleet:join { fleet, as:'leader' }` in one call) — BEFORE you orient or plan. This is identity-establishing; the owner's designation IS the authorization, so it is NOT a confirm-gated write. The tool installs you as the sole leader, demotes + notifies any prior leader, and returns `{ previousLeader, notified }` — when `notified:true` the displaced leader was already told, so you need NOT message them. Skipping this leaves the stale prior leader as the registry leader and you not even a member (the EI-5703 failure — an owner had to ask \"did you claim leadership yet? why not?\").\n\n1. Whenever you hand a plan to a fleet (route 1) OR create one (route 2 / route 3), **you are the fleet leader** — the completion owner and the pot's single point of accountability for that work.\n2. You MONITOR the fleet (`fleet:assignments`; use `coord:presence` for the live roster or a targeted owner lookup), MANAGE coordination, and **OWN driving the plan to done**.\n3. Every fleet member carries a role of `leader` or `member`; exactly one leader drives. Delegating is taking the leader seat, not vacating responsibility.\n4. **Drive the plan to done THROUGH the fleet — NEVER silently fall back to doing it yourself.** \"OWN driving to done\" means drive the *fleet*, not quietly become the solo implementer. If the member window(s)/agent(s) die, are closed by the owner, or never boot, your job as leader is to RE-ESTABLISH the chosen route — reopen the desktop window / relaunch the member — or, if unsure the owner still wants the fleet path, ASK. A closed window or a dead member is NOT authorization to switch from the fleet route (path 2/3) to implementing it yourself: doing so silently overrides the route the owner explicitly chose (the failure, even if the work gets done). Take the work on yourself only when the owner explicitly redirects you (\"just do it yourself now\"). Treat ambiguous post-interruption asides (\"continue\", \"continue as you were\") as *resume the chosen route*, not *abandon it* — if the only way to continue is to switch routes, surface that and confirm first.\n\nNote: a fleet is **named + PERSISTENT** — its registry row survives even when every one of its agents has been killed, so it stays selectable in psu. \"Available\" means something narrower: it currently has ≥1 LIVE member (a recent presence heartbeat). A killed-empty fleet is still selectable but is NOT \"available\" for path 2.\n\n<!--PSU_CACHE_BOUNDARY-->\n\n# Operating brief — this launch\n\n> Generated from the selected scope and plan. This compact index points into\n> the full playbook; it does not replace its safety rules.\n\n<!-- papercusp-rule:harness-scope=explicit-per-call -->\n- **Scope:** harness `papercusp`; pass `harness: 'papercusp'` to `features:*`, `issues:*`, and `plans:*`.\n- **Papercusp engineering docs:** for `docs:*` reads of `agent-insights/*` and framework docs, pass `harness: 'all'` in an unscoped operator session; workspace-scoped sessions use `harness: 'engineering'` instead.\n- **Other harnesses:** read through `cross_harness:docs_*` / `cross_harness:plans_*`.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:test-router=test-file -->\n- **Exact tests:** Vitest files use `npm run test:file -- <test paths>`, which routes each file to its owning Vitest config; registered non-Vitest files (for example `papercusp-desktop` Node tests) use their package's documented runner because `test:file` is Vitest-only.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:app-runtime=tauri -->\n- **UI verification:** drive the Tauri shell; server-side staging changes run on `:3170`.\n<!-- papercusp-rule:git-ownership=background-sync -->\n- **Git:** leave verified edits in `staging`; the background sync owns commit and push.\n\n---\n## Launch Context\n\n# Fleet member — operating baseline\n\nYou are one of 20 parallel worker agents in fleet `nonp2p-feature-drain-sol61-xhigh-0930`, draining your fleet claim-lane backlog. The session that launched you is your LEADER — report notable completions and blockers to them.\n\nLoop: **pull** with `scheduler:get_next { harness: '<your-harness>' }` (`heldPaths`; `states` only when filtering and only `open|failing`; never pass retired `todo` or floor/terminal states; `rigAvailable`; omit `specId`/`revision`; inspect `claimedUnder`; leader steers via `scheduler:set_claim_spec`; NOT `work_items:claim_next`; PICKUP is yours) → **read** with `work_items:get` → **act** → terminal evidence → repeat. Do NOT self-prioritize by scanning `work_items:list`.\n\n## Non-negotiables\n1. **Already-fixed check FIRST.** Before building, spend ~2 min checking code/tests, `git log`, and sibling work-items for an existing fix. If it shipped, close as already-fixed WITH that evidence; do not rebuild it.\n2. **STAY ALIVE across turns — loop:arm at spawn, not park.** No human is at your keyboard: FIRST call `loop:arm { intervalSec, goal, carry: 'warm' }`. Each wake, `scheduler:get_next` → work to terminal (`work_items:complete`) → repeat. Call `loop:end { acknowledgeOpenDirectives:true, acknowledgeWakeLessAutonomy:true }` only when no claimable work remains or you are blocked; otherwise ending without the loop parks you until a leader wake (EI-8318).\n3. **Flag to your LEADER; keep status in your FLEET, not the whole hive.** Send blockers, systemic findings, and \"nothing left to claim\" to the leader (`wakeOnReply:true`) — broadcast is easy to miss. A finding >1 paragraph goes on the item, not chat; `coord:read {msg_id}` gets its full text. In-fleet: bare to:[\"*\"] auto-scopes `@fleet:<slug>`; `allHive:true` only for system-wide news.\n4. **Do not re-claim a ping-ponging item.** Releasing an item bumps its `updated_at`, so it can re-surface at the top of next `scheduler:get_next` pull and loop on it. If an item reappears right after you release it, sink it (work_items:set_priority) or set it `blocked` with a reason — do not re-claim.\n5. **Completion evidence is mandatory.** `work_items:complete` needs `{id,state,assumptions: \"none\",completion:{summary,testsRun,testResult,verifiedHow,filesChanged}}`; fact keys may replace `\"none\"`. Successful bug/capability-gap closes also need `completion.rootCauseVerification:{hypothesis,alternativeHypothesis,distinguishingTest,testResult,testProcedure,predictedObservations:{hypothesis:\"<H1>\",alternativeHypothesis:\"<H2>\"},actualObservation,evidenceRefs}`. The typed predictions must differ; `distinguishingTest` requires no prose template.\n6. **\"Not available\" means DEFERRED, not missing.** InputValidationError/\"not available\" means load the tool (ToolSearch/tools:find) and continue; never report it missing.\n7. **Edit only the staging tree; git-sync owns commit + push.** Never git add/commit/push. If a file lock blocks an edit, pivot rather than route around it.\n8. **A hive pause is a Mug-loop signal, not a self-drain order.** `pauseNewWork` / `maxBees` / a pot-steering fact you SEE in orient governs the autonomous mug-cup loop — do NOT stop your claimed work on it. Wind down only on a graceful-drain cue ADDRESSED to you (check its authority+scope stamp: `hive-queen(<hive>)→hive-wide` is the Mug; a `fleet-leader(<other>)→fleet-members` cue is a DIFFERENT fleet's business — ignore it) or an explicit `fleet:*`/owner action. Unsure? Ask your leader, never self-drain on an observed pause.\n9. **Turn-end reflection + reporting integrity.** End each turn with ONE bounded reflection: file an observation (`improvements:capture lane:\"observation\"`) ONLY if the turn surfaced something a FUTURE agent benefits from — a routine turn records NOTHING (a sensor reading, never a fix or self-grade). Never fabricate a signal: a truthful `blocked` beats a fabricated all-clear — never report a state you weren't in, a send you didn't make, or a reading you didn't take.\n10. **Carry-note checkpoint at every boundary.** Write `work_items:checkpoint { id, checkpoint }` at task completion, before going idle at a task boundary, and on graceful-evict — so your successor resumes mid-thread instead of cold. Content = what you accomplished / what is left / the key insight / a gotcha for your successor; concrete facts, not self-evaluation; a compact digest, never a transcript. Replace-on-write (blank to clear).\n\n---\n\n# Fleet-specific brief (from your leader — wins on specifics)\n\nAvi-authorized current-capacity restoration under nonp2p-feature-queue-cleanup-2026-10-03#D-006; join only existing fleet nonp2p-feature-drain-sol61-xhigh-0930. You are a feature implementation MEMBER, not an audit/acceptance leader. Preserve inherited exact claim-spec revision6, maxConcurrentClaims1, every P2P/shared-hive/federation and solo-owner exclusion; never set a member spec, broaden scope, force a claim or take the separately owned PERSONAL cleanup/METHOD/instrument/vetting work. Keep headless Codex GPT-6.1 Sol at xhigh, unpinned inference-gateway auto and warm carry, session AUTO. On this initial restoration turn verify identity, actual native model/effort/account route, membership and effective cupId:self claim spec, then make ONE supported scheduler:get_next pull on qualified staging3170 with the unchanged inherited scope. The evidence-only judge role is intentionally excluded from coordination-write\\n  tools, so it must not call coord:declare-intent, claim plan lanes, or pass intent to\\n  coord:orient (that causes an internal declaration attempt). Judges may call coord:orient\\n  {} without intent for omitted read context, then work only the item already routed to\\n  them. This omits memory recall and intent declaration by design.\\n\\n  **ROUTE A — an `## Orientation` block already arrived in this turn.** Your held\\n  work-items, unanswered directed messages, and whether a wake source (armed loop)\\n  exists came WITH it: the server read them for you. Do NOT spend a\\n  `coord:orient` round-trip re-fetching them — you are oriented. Claim your lane\\n  with `coord:declare-intent { intent, items }`, and reach for\\n  `coord:orient` only for what that block deliberately EXCLUDES: the claimable\\n  backlog, full inbox bodies, a mem0 recall. Judge by PRESENCE ONLY — the block is\\n  emitted just when that state CHANGES, and only to hosts that inject it, so its\\n  ABSENCE never means \\\"you are oriented\\\".\\n\\n  **ROUTE B — no such block.** Bootstrap in ONE call:\\n  **`coord:orient { intent }`** — pass your one-line intent for the\\n  task. In a SINGLE round-trip it returns your current assignments\\n  (+ lane + load), the claimable backlog, your unread inbox summary,\\n  the recent plan-events delta, AND a mem0 recall for `intent` — and\\n  it DECLARES `intent` to peers so they see what you're working on.\\n  After a SUCCESSFUL orient, do NOT separately call `coord:plan-events`,\\n  `memory:search`, `coord:inbox`, or `coord:declare-intent` — orient's\\n  result ALREADY contains them (plan-events delta + inbox summary + a mem0\\n  recall) and ALREADY declared your intent; re-calling them just re-pays the\\n  round-trip orient collapsed. Reach for one individually only for a detail\\n  orient deliberately bounds (full inbox bodies, or a mem0 query OTHER than\\n  your intent).\\n\\n  - **Claim your lane.** When the work is plan items, pass them:\\n    `coord:orient { intent, planSlug, planItems: ['P-001', …] }` CLAIMS\\n    those items for you (and releases ones you've moved off). An unclaimed\\n    lane is invisible to the Mug and peers, so work gets double-placed.\\n    (Flipping an item `wip` via `plans:set-status` also auto-claims;\\n    `done` releases. A `claim_conflict` means a live peer holds it —\\n    coordinate with the holder, don't take it.)\\n  - **mem0 (what you know).** orient's recall uses `intent` as the query;\\n    pass `harness` for project-specific facts. Each mem0 hit carries an\\n    `id` — if the user later contradicts something, `memory:forget`\\n    that id. Use `memoryQuery` for a different query, or call\\n    `memory:search` directly. A recall hit is BINDING context, not flavor:\\n    if a recalled fact prescribes a behavior for THIS task, follow it — or\\n    explicitly say why you're not.\\n  - **insights (how things work).** When you hit a confusing failure,\\n    `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section before grepping code —\\n    many \\\"weird bugs\\\" already have a written runbook.\\n  - **State answers NOW; only the append-only log answers EVER.** `coord:presence` /\\n    `fleet:assignments` are LIVE-STATE — who is alive, who holds what RIGHT NOW; an ended\\n    agent loses its fleet_slug and its presence row is TTL-reaped, so they CANNOT answer an\\n    *ever / was / missed / history* question. Route those to `coord:catch-up { audience }`\\n    (as a member of the fleet/topic) or `coord:feed { audience }` (the firehose) instead —\\n    never a state tool. Full map:\\n    `docs:search` `agent-insights/presence-vs-history-who-is-on-what`.\\n\\nRight layer for READS and WRITES — the memory↔docs boundary:\\n  - **HOW IT WORKS** (a runbook, a failure mode, why-something-is, a hard-won gotcha):\\n    READ via `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section; WRITE a new/updated MDX under\\n    `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/` with a `documents:` frontmatter\\n    anchor to the code it describes. This is the RIGHT place — a doc is code-ANCHORED,\\n    drift-TRACKED (the freshness sweep) and AUTO-HEALED (the doc-steward); a mem0 vector cannot\\n    be anchored/swept/auto-rewritten, so how-it-works left only in mem0 silently rots. Do NOT\\n    park a runbook in mem0.\\n  - **WHY a subsystem/decision is the way it is** (the rationale behind a design, not how it works):\\n    READ via `rationale:feed { topic }` — a topic-keyed projection over the relevant\\n    plan-decisions + work-items + insights, kept fresh by the event engine (`topics:list` for the\\n    topic, then `plans:get`/`docs:get` on an entry's `ref` for the full text). The discoverable\\n    \\\"why\\\" layer — reach for it before grepping plans/decisions by hand.\\n  - **A durable PERSONAL/PREFERENCE fact** (who the user is, a convention, an owner pref):\\n    READ via `memory:search`; WRITE via `memory:remember`. Keep mem0 entries SHORT, and when\\n    the why already lives in a doc/plan store only the non-derivable fact + a POINTER\\n    (`[[<plan-slug>]]`, `/internal/docs/agent-insights/<slug>`), never a copied paragraph.\\n  - **In-flight state** → coord; **derivable session state** (X shipped, migration N, N tests)\\n    → the plan / work-item, never memory.\\nSee the plans `papercusp-su-memory-2026-05-25` and\\n`tool-call-batching-wrappers-2026-06-21`.\\n\\n## Your tool surface is DYNAMIC — the whole 959-tool catalog is reachable on demand\\n\\nYour loaded tool list is usually a small CORE set (the default). An unclaimed\\n    lane is invisible to the Mug and peers, so work gets double-placed.\\n    (Flipping an item `wip` via `plans:set-status` also auto-claims;\\n    `done` releases. Route those to `coord:catch-up { audience }`\\n    (as a member of the fleet/topic) or `coord:feed { audience }` (the firehose) instead —\\n    never a state tool. A leader who just called scheduler:set_claim_spec had no\n * tool-surface way to confirm the re-steer actually landed before relying on it. Trivial read\n * projection over claim-spec-store's getClaimSpecRecord (bee spec → fleet spec → DEFAULT).\n */\nimport { z } from 'zod';\nimport { defineTool } from '@papercusp/agent-mcp';\nimport { resolveAgentIdentity } from '../coordination/identity';\nimport { COORD_ROLES } from '../coordination/roles';\nimport { resolveClaimSpecWorkspace, getClaimSpecRecord, fleetSpecBeeKey } from '../../scheduler/claim-spec-store';\nimport {\n  readClaimSpecRevisions,\n  claimSpecHistoryElsewhereHint,\n  CLAIM_SPEC_HISTORY_MAX,\n} from '../../scheduler/claim-spec-revisions';\nimport { fleetSentinelCallerView } from './fleet-sentinel-caller-view';\n\nexport default defineTool({\n  name: 'scheduler:get_claim_spec',\n  profile: 'engineer',\n  description:\n    'Read the CURRENT claim spec for a cup or fleet: { source, spec, revision, updatedBy, updatedAt, harnessSlug, fleetSlug? }. `source` tells you which row actually answered — \"bee\" (a per-bee spec, always wins), \"fleet\" (inherited via membership, no per-bee override), or \"default\" (neither exists — DEFAULT_CLAIM_SPEC/oldest-first applies). The read counterpart to scheduler:set_claim_spec — confirm a re-steer landed before relying on it, instead of grepping source or guessing. Pass `history: N` to also get up to N PRIOR versions a destructive write superseded; use `history: 0` for an explicitly bounded current-only read.',\n  guidance: {\n    when:\n      'You just called scheduler:set_claim_spec and want to confirm the write landed (right revision, right filter/rank) — or you want to know WHAT spec a bee/fleet is currently running under before re-steering it. This is a selector-only read: pass exactly one of cupId | fleet, plus optional workspace; do not forward generic harness or planSlug context from coord:orient or fleet wake discovery because those keys are rejected.',\n    notWhen:\n      'Setting/replacing a spec — scheduler:set_claim_spec. What is executing right now under which spec (the live-execution view across many bees) — scheduler:running. Full fleet roster / orphaned-claim detection — fleet:assignments.',\n    chaining: 'scheduler:get_claim_spec (confirm current) → scheduler:set_claim_spec (re-steer) → scheduler:get_claim_spec (confirm the bump landed).',\n    seeAlso: [\n      // EI-20185841251188914: the scope-arg matrix across the spec-addressing trio, stated\n      // on each member so a caller reading any ONE of them learns the distinction. Derived\n      // truth, pinned by scope-args-contract.test.ts — edit that test WITH any arg change.\n      // Lives in seeAlso (and not in when/notWhen/chaining) because seeAlso is outside the\n      // per-tool prompt-weight budget: this tool sits at ~1408 of 1500 chars, and the same\n      // sentence in `when` reds the fleet gate.\n      'scheduler:set_claim_spec (write/re-steer a spec — MIRROR SCOPE ARGS: it takes harness and NO workspace, this read takes workspace and NO harness, so do not copy a scope key across the get→set→get chain)',\n      'scheduler:preview_spec_delta (dry-run a revision — the scope superset: cupId|fleet plus BOTH harness and workspace)',\n      'scheduler:running (live-execution view across many bees)',\n      'fleet:assignments (full fleet roster)',\n    ],\n    // A caller reaching this tool almost always arrives from `coord:orient` or a fleet\n    // wake, both of which hand them a `harness` in context — and the natural move is to\n    // forward it. `when` already says not to, in the same sentence that names the\n    // accepted selectors, and the filings kept coming: catalog prose is not on the\n    // FAILURE path, which is the only moment the caller is holding the rejected key.\n    //\n    // The trap this must not repeat is specific: the WRITE half of the same chain,\n    // scheduler:set_claim_spec, DOES take `harness` and takes no `workspace`. So the\n    // rejection cannot simply be read as \"harness scoping does not exist here\" — a\n    // caller who concludes that will drop it from the set call too and re-steer the\n    // wrong partition. The note therefore names the asymmetry, not just the remedy.\n    //\n    // Object (corrective-call) form because there is no local key a harness VALUE could\n    // be relocated onto: `fleet` takes a fleet slug, not a harness slug, so a\n    // `fleet — explanation` string would render \"pass it as `fleet` instead\" over a\n    // value that would then be rejected a second time.\n    argRedirects: {\n      harness: {\n        tool: 'scheduler:get_claim_spec',\n        args: { fleet: '<fleet-slug>' },\n        note:\n          'this READ is selector-only — exactly ONE of `cupId` (one cup, with fleet inheritance) or `fleet` (a fleet\\'s own sentinel spec); a harness is not a selector here. ⚠ Do NOT conclude harness scoping is absent from the family: the WRITE verb scheduler:set_claim_spec DOES take `harness` and takes NO `workspace`, exactly inverted from this read — so drop `harness` here, and keep it there. To override the partition on this read, use `workspace`',\n      },\n      planSlug: {\n        tool: 'scheduler:get_claim_spec',\n        args: { fleet: '<fleet-slug>' },\n        note:\n          'a claim spec is addressed by WHO runs it (a cup or a fleet), never by the plan it happens to be working — one fleet\\'s spec can admit several plans, so a plan slug cannot identify a spec row. Pass `fleet` (or `cupId`). For \"who is on plan P\" use fleet:assignments { plan }',\n      },\n      // EI-21659569223378788 / EI-21825767595982783: a claim RECEIPT surfaces `specId`,\n      // so the natural read-back is to hand that same id straight to this tool. It is\n      // rejected, and the caller is left holding an identifier the read verb cannot\n      // consume. The spec row is addressed by its OWNER, never by its own id — the id\n      // identifies a revision, and revisions are reached through `history`, not selected.\n      specId: {\n        tool: 'scheduler:get_claim_spec',\n        args: { fleet: '<fleet-slug>' },\n        note:\n          'a spec is addressed by WHOSE it is, not by its own id — there is no by-id read. A `specId` off a claim receipt cannot be handed back here: translate it to the owner it belongs to (the receipt reports the fleet/cup alongside it) and pass `fleet` or `cupId`. To see PRIOR revisions of that lane rather than the current one, add `history: N` to the same owner-addressed call',\n      },\n      spec: {\n        tool: 'scheduler:get_claim_spec',\n        args: { fleet: '<fleet-slug>' },\n        note:\n          'this is the READ verb — it RETURNS the spec, it does not take one. Address the lane you want to read with `fleet` or `cupId`. If you meant to WRITE a spec, that is scheduler:set_claim_spec (which takes `harness`, not `workspace` — the scope args are inverted between the two)',\n      },\n      // EI-21834535376765161: a goal-NAMED fleet makes the goal id look like a selector.\n      // It is not — the fleet slug is, and the two are routinely different strings.\n      goalId: {\n        tool: 'scheduler:get_claim_spec',\n        args: { fleet: '<fleet-slug>' },\n        note:\n          'a goal is not a claim-spec selector, even when the fleet running it is named after the goal — the fleet SLUG is the selector and is often a different string. Resolve the goal to its fleet (fleet:assignments, or the `fleetSlug` your own coord:orient reports) and pass that as `fleet`',\n      },\n    },\n  },\n  capability: 'work_items:read',\n  requirePrincipal: false,\n  // EI-20228676874653267: this read uses the claim-spec store's own DB access\n  // and never reads ctx.tx. Keeping the dispatcher's ambient transaction open\n  // while resolving the spec pins an org-app pool slot and lets concurrent\n  // fleet-control reads queue behind the 45s acquisition deadline.\n  skipWorkspaceTx: true,\n  agentRoles: [...COORD_ROLES],\n  args: z\n    .object({\n      // EI-21268733197990138 / EI-21297588777075247 / EI-21391324675237501 /\n      // EI-21571638267356829: both selectors are `.optional()` in the projected JSON\n      // schema — which is the only truthful encoding of \"exactly one of\", since neither\n      // is required on its own — so a caller reading the schema sees two optional fields\n      // and reasonably calls with NEITHER (or both). The exactly-one rule lives in a\n      // .refine() that the schema cannot express, so each field's own describe() is the\n      // only place a caller meets it BEFORE the failure. Say it on both, not just cupId.\n      cupId: z\n        .string()\n        .min(1)\n        .optional()\n        .describe(\n          'the concrete session/owner id to read. The literal \"self\" is not a selector here; use coord:whoami to get your ownerId. REQUIRED-EXACTLY-ONE of cupId | fleet — both are marked optional here only because either may be the one you pass; a call with NEITHER, or with BOTH, is rejected',\n        ),\n      fleet: z\n        .string()\n        .min(1)\n        .optional()\n        .describe(\n          'a fleet slug — reads the fleet-level sentinel spec directly (not a member\\'s inherited view). REQUIRED-EXACTLY-ONE of cupId | fleet (see cupId). A fleet MEMBER reading its own lane passes its own fleet slug here — coord:orient reports it as `fleetSlug`; there is no implicit \"my fleet\" default, because this read is also how you inspect a fleet you are NOT in',\n        ),\n      workspace: z.string().max(120).optional().describe('override the workspace partition (default: resolved from your identity)'),\n      history: z\n        .number()\n        .int()\n        .min(0)\n        .max(CLAIM_SPEC_HISTORY_MAX)\n        .optional()\n        // EI-21918830080331891 / EI-21265931516384958: both callers passed `history: true`,\n        // meaning \"yes, include history\". The name is a NOUN and reads as a flag, and the\n        // bare Zod refusal (\"expected number, received boolean\") states the type without\n        // stating the COUNT semantics — so the obvious repair from that message alone is\n        // `history: 1`, which silently returns one prior version instead of the several\n        // the caller wanted. Say the count, and say what `true` should have been.\n        .describe(\n          `also return up to N (max ${CLAIM_SPEC_HISTORY_MAX}) PRIOR versions of this lane, newest first — the spec bytes a destructive write superseded, enough to rebuild it; 0 returns the current spec without prior versions. This is a COUNT, not a flag: pass a number, and if you meant \\`history: true\\` (\"include the history\") you want \\`history: ${CLAIM_SPEC_HISTORY_MAX}\\` — the max — not \\`1\\`, which returns a single prior version`,\n        ),\n    })\n    // The refusal text is the ONLY surface a caller meets at the moment they are holding\n    // the bad call, and the old message named the rule without naming a remedy — so the\n    // two failing populations (no selector at all, and both at once) both read it as a\n    // restatement of the schema they had just misread. Branch on which mistake was made\n    // and name the concrete next call for each.\n    .refine((a) => Boolean(a.cupId) !== Boolean(a.fleet), {\n      // Zod 4: the branch goes in `error` (a function), not in the params position —\n      // `.refine(check, (val) => params)` is a Zod 3 form and does not typecheck here.\n      error: (iss) => {\n        const passedBoth = Boolean((iss.input as { cupId?: unknown } | undefined)?.cupId);\n        return passedBoth\n          ? 'pass exactly ONE of cupId or fleet — you passed BOTH. They are different questions: cupId reads ONE cup (with fleet inheritance applied), fleet reads a fleet\\'s OWN sentinel spec. Drop whichever you did not mean; to see what a cup actually runs under, keep cupId'\n          : 'pass exactly ONE of cupId (read one cup, with fleet inheritance) or fleet (read a fleet\\'s own sentinel spec) — you passed NEITHER, and there is no implicit \"my own lane\" default. If you are a fleet member reading your own lane, pass your own fleet slug (coord:orient reports it as `fleetSlug`); to read one cup, pass cupId';\n      },\n    }),\n  async handler(args, ctx) {\n    const ident = resolveAgentIdentity(ctx);\n    const requestedCupId = args.cupId;\n    if (requestedCupId?.trim() === 'self') {\n      throw Object.assign(\n        new Error(\n          `cupId must be a concrete session/owner ID, not the literal \"self\". To read your own claim spec, use { cupId: '${ident.ownerId}' } for this session.`,\n        ),\n        { code: 'invalid_claim_spec_selector' },\n      );\n    }\n    const workspaceId = resolveClaimSpecWorkspace(args.workspace ?? ident.workspaceId);\n    const fleetSlug = args.fleet ? args.fleet.trim() : null;\n    const targetCupId = fleetSlug ? fleetSpecBeeKey(fleetSlug) : (requestedCupId as string);\n    const record = await getClaimSpecRecord({ cupId: targetCupId, workspaceId });\n\n    // EI-20304090779240149: a fleet read answers about the FLEET, and its envelope is\n    // shaped exactly like the caller-scoped cupId read — so \"source: fleet, rev 7\" was\n    // being taken as \"I am running under rev 7\" by callers who were in no fleet at all,\n    // which then took out-of-lane work on the next self-pull. Resolve the CALLER too and\n    // say plainly whether this sentinel is their effective spec. Best-effort: the caller\n    // view never fails the read (an unreadable comparison reports UNKNOWN, never\n    // agreement). Only for the fleet selector — a cupId read is already unambiguous\n    // about whose spec it returned.\n    const callerView = fleetSlug\n      ? fleetSentinelCallerView({\n          fleetSlug,\n          callerId: ident.ownerId,\n          callerRecord: await getClaimSpecRecord({ cupId: ident.ownerId, workspaceId }).catch(\n            () => null,\n          ),\n        })\n      : null;\n    const subject = fleetSlug\n      ? { subject: { kind: 'fleet-sentinel' as const, fleetSlug }, ...callerView }\n      : {};\n\n    if (args.history === undefined || args.history === 0) {\n      return { data: { ok: true, ...record, ...subject } };\n    }\n    // History is read for the target the CALLER ADDRESSED, not for whichever row answered\n    // the current-spec read. The read counterpart to scheduler:set_claim_spec — confirm a re-steer landed before relying on it, instead of grepping source or guessing. {"timestamp":"2026-10-09T13:05:49.993Z","ordinal":66,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a120c1-5653-7203-abef-84b1f05ed29b","turn_id":"01a120c1-bd48-72c3-b0d7-d0bb8e38c9a3","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-208d3afd-4d20-413a-ace1-25a9af5004d4","process_id":"79754","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '1,200p' libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/codex-gateway-config.ts\n"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '1,200p' libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/codex-gateway-config.ts","name":"codex-gateway-config.ts","path":"libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/codex-gateway-config.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"/**\n * codex-gateway-config.ts — the ONE codex inference-gateway config.toml builder (WI-3645).\n *\n * Renders the `model_provider` blocks that point a codex CLI session at the localhost\n * Papercusp inference gateway. Consumed by BOTH codex config writers:\n *   • `spawn-mcp.ts` `writeSignedSpawnCodexHome` (same package) — SPAWNED agents\n *     (fleet members, bees; env-driven via PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ID / PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY);\n *   • operator-core `role-codex-home.ts` (via the `@papercusp/orchestrator/codex-gateway-config`\n *     subpath export) — the INTERACTIVE psu path (resolveAccountPin / bootstrap-su).\n *\n * Before this extraction each writer carried its own near-identical copy, and they DRIFTED:\n * the spawned copy learned unpinned auto-routing (WI-3645) while the interactive copy still\n * required a pin — which is exactly how \"auto\" stayed unwired interactively. One builder,\n * one behavior. (Owner directive 2026-07-09: \"share as much code as possible with the claude\n * implementation, abstracting away the model specific things into shared code\" — the claude\n * analogue is operator-core's `gatewaySpawnEnv`, which likewise routes pin-or-no-pin.)\n *\n * ROUTING SEMANTICS (mirrors the claude path):\n *   • `accountId` set   → gateway config WITH the `x-papercusp-account` pin header.\n *   • `gatewayOn` set   → gateway config WITHOUT the pin header (explicit-auto / unpinned):\n *     the gateway's own codex handling auto-selects — bearer pool first, then the codex-CLI\n *     account fallback — when no account header is present. The header is OMITTED entirely,\n *     never emitted empty (an empty pin would name a nonexistent account and 4xx).\n *   • neither           → `{ root: [], tables: [] }` (gateway off; direct egress unchanged).\n *\n * The `# BEGIN/END PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY_*` marker lines are LOAD-BEARING: config writers\n * and diagnostics locate/replace the managed blocks by them — keep them byte-stable.\n */\n\n/**\n * The one provider id every managed codex config names. Exported because it is\n * not just a config-writing detail: codex stamps it into each rollout's\n * `session_meta.model_provider` and re-resolves it against the CURRENT config at\n * `thread/resume`, so the RESUME path has to recognise a thread that is bound to\n * it and refuse to strip the table (WI-38706). One constant, both readers.\n */\nexport const CODEX_GATEWAY_PROVIDER_ID = 'papercusp-codex-gateway';\n\n/** Escape a value for a TOML double-quoted basic string. */\nexport function tomlEscape(s: string): string {\n  return s.replace(/\\\\/g, '\\\\\\\\').replace(/\"/g, '\\\\\"');\n}\n\n/** The localhost gateway port (PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_PORT override → default 8788). */\nexport function codexGatewayPort(): number {\n  const p = Number(process.env.PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_PORT);\n  return Number.isFinite(p) && p > 0 ? p : 8788;\n}\n\nexport interface CodexGatewayConfigOpts {\n  /** Gateway attribution/owner header (x-papercusp-owner) — the spawn/session owner id. */\n  ownerId?: string | null;\n  /** Admission-tier label (x-papercusp-priority) — the spawn role, when the tier flag resolved one. */\n  priority?: string | null;\n  /** Route through the gateway even with NO account pin (explicit-auto / unpinned).\n   *  Ignored when `accountId` is set (a pin implies the gateway). */\n  gatewayOn?: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Feature policy baked into every Papercusp-managed CODEX_HOME.\n *\n * Codex 0.147 enables `remote_compaction_v2` by default. That native path cuts\n * the conversation before Papercusp can write a carry note or deliberately\n * restart the session, so managed sessions disable it and use\n * `session:request-compaction` instead. Interactive role/SU homes also disable\n * Codex's native memory store; short-lived spawn homes preserve their existing\n * memory setting by passing `disableMemories: false`.\n */\nexport function codexManagedFeaturesToml(\n  opts: { disableMemories?: boolean; headless?: boolean } = {},\n): string[] {\n  return [\n    // CLI versions are managed outside startup. An update dialog can block a\n    // carry-respawn before it creates its native session or accepts wakes.\n    'check_for_update_on_startup = false',\n    '# Papercusp owns context carry/restart; Codex native compaction must not cut first.',\n    '[features]',\n    ...(opts.disableMemories === false ? [] : ['memories = false']),\n    'remote_compaction_v2 = false',\n    // Custom providers do not consult `model_catalog_url` unless this Codex feature is on.\n    // Without it, /model silently falls back to the shared/default-account cache even while\n    // the gateway can serve newer model ids for inference.\n    'api_key_model_discovery = true',\n    // A headless managed PTY has no human who can answer Codex's plugin/app\n    // authentication elicitation. Leaving plugins enabled makes a 401 from the\n    // remote ChatGPT plugin catalog start an OAuth browser flow for every fleet\n    // member, even when model inference uses an API key or custom provider and\n    // needs no ChatGPT login. Suppress that optional interactive surface only\n    // for headless sessions; visible sessions keep the ordinary plugin UX.\n    ...(opts.headless\n      ? [\n          'plugins = false',\n          'auth_elicitation = false',\n        ]\n      : []),\n    '',\n  ];\n}\n\n/**\n * The managed gateway blocks for a codex `config.toml`: `root` lines (top-level\n * `model_provider = …`) and `tables` lines (the `[model_providers.…]` table).\n * Empty when neither a pin nor `gatewayOn` asked for the gateway.\n */\nexport function codexGatewayConfigToml(\n  accountId?: string | null,\n  opts: CodexGatewayConfigOpts = {},\n): { root: string[]; tables: string[] } {\n  const pinnedAccount = accountId?.trim();\n  // WI-3645: a pin gets routing config as before; a caller that passes NO pin but sets\n  // `gatewayOn` (the explicit-auto / unpinned case) ALSO gets routing config, just without the\n  // account-pin header — the gateway's own codex fallback auto-selects when the header is\n  // absent. Only a caller that passes neither (gateway fully off) gets no config.\n  if (!pinnedAccount && !opts.gatewayOn) return { root: [], tables: [] };\n  const providerId = CODEX_GATEWAY_PROVIDER_ID;\n  // `/v1/models` is shared by the Claude and Codex adapters. Inference is\n  // unambiguous from `/v1/responses`, but the native model-catalog client does\n  // not stamp Codex's usual originator header. Make the provider identity\n  // explicit so an unpinned `account=auto` catalog request cannot fall through\n  // to Claude's differently-shaped `{ data: [...] }` response.\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = { originator: 'codex_cli_rs' };\n  if (pinnedAccount) headers['x-papercusp-account'] = pinnedAccount;\n  const ownerId = opts.ownerId?.trim();\n  if (ownerId) headers['x-papercusp-owner'] = ownerId;\n  const priority = opts.priority?.trim();\n  if (priority) headers['x-papercusp-priority'] = priority;\n  const gatewayBaseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${codexGatewayPort()}`;\n  const headerEntries = Object.entries(headers);\n  const httpHeadersLine = headerEntries.length\n    ? [`http_headers = { ${headerEntries.map(([k, v]) => `\"${tomlEscape(k)}\" = \"${tomlEscape(v)}\"`).join(', ')} }`]\n    : [];\n  return {\n    root: [\n      '# BEGIN PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY_ROOT',\n      '# Route Codex model traffic through the Papercusp inference gateway account pin.',\n      `model_provider = \"${providerId}\"`,\n      '# END PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY_ROOT',\n      '',\n    ],\n    tables: [\n      '# BEGIN PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY_PROVIDER',\n      `[model_providers.${providerId}]`,\n      'name = \"Papercusp Codex Gateway\"',\n      `base_url = \"${gatewayBaseUrl}/v1\"`,\n      // Codex model discovery is a distinct provider endpoint. {"timestamp":"2026-10-09T13:05:52.854Z","ordinal":71,"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call_output","id":"ctco_01a120c5-22d5-73d0-a0cf-e6a73656bb57","call_id":"call_4d775c770f344747ba8f519878ea9c55","output":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Script completed\nWall time 3.3 seconds\nOutput:\n"},{"type":"input_text","text":"{\"i\":0,\"result\":{\"status\":\"fulfilled\",\"value\":{\"chunk_id\":\"540b8d\",\"wall_time_seconds\":0.000061679,\"exit_code\":0,\"original_token_count\":2090,\"output\":\"/**\\n * codex-gateway-config.ts — the ONE codex inference-gateway config.toml builder (WI-3645).\\n *\\n * Renders the `model_provider` blocks that point a codex CLI session at the localhost\\n * Papercusp inference gateway. Consumed by BOTH codex config writers:\\n *   • `spawn-mcp.ts` `writeSignedSpawnCodexHome` (same package) — SPAWNED agents\\n *     (fleet members, bees; env-driven via PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ID / PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY);\\n *   • operator-core `role-codex-home.ts` (via the `@papercusp/orchestrator/codex-gateway-config`\\n *     subpath export) — the INTERACTIVE psu path (resolveAccountPin / bootstrap-su).\\n *\\n * Before this extraction each writer carried its own near-identical copy, and they DRIFTED:\\n * the spawned copy learned unpinned auto-routing (WI-3645) while the interactive copy still\\n * required a pin — which is exactly how \\\"auto\\\" stayed unwired interactively. One builder,\\n * one behavior. (Owner directive 2026-07-09: \\\"share as much code as possible with the claude\\n * implementation, abstracting away the model specific things into shared code\\\" — the claude\\n * analogue is operator-core's `gatewaySpawnEnv`, which likewise routes pin-or-no-pin.)\\n *\\n * ROUTING SEMANTICS (mirrors the claude path):\\n *   • `accountId` set   → gateway config WITH the `x-papercusp-account` pin header.\\n *   • `gatewayOn` set   → gateway config WITHOUT the pin header (explicit-auto / unpinned):\\n *     the gateway's own codex handling auto-selects — bearer pool first, then the codex-CLI\\n *     account fallback — when no account header is present. The header is OMITTED entirely,\\n *     never emitted empty (an empty pin would name a nonexistent account and 4xx).\\n *   • neither           → `{ root: [], tables: [] }` (gateway off; direct egress unchanged).\\n *\\n * The `# BEGIN/END PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY_*` marker lines are LOAD-BEARING: config writers\\n * and diagnostics locate/replace the managed blocks by them — keep them byte-stable.\\n */\\n\\n/**\\n * The one provider id every managed codex config names. Exported because it is\\n * not just a config-writing detail: codex stamps it into each rollout's\\n * `session_meta.model_provider` and re-resolves it against the CURRENT config at\\n * `thread/resume`, so the RESUME path has to recognise a thread that is bound to\\n * it and refuse to strip the table (WI-38706). One constant, both readers.\\n */\\nexport const CODEX_GATEWAY_PROVIDER_ID = 'papercusp-codex-gateway';\\n\\n/** Escape a value for a TOML double-quoted basic string. */\\nexport function tomlEscape(s: string): string {\\n  return s.replace(/\\\\\\\\/g, '\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\').replace(/\\\"/g, '\\\\\\\\\\\"');\\n}\\n\\n/** The localhost gateway port (PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_PORT override → default 8788). */\\nexport function codexGatewayPort(): number {\\n  const p = Number(process.env.PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_PORT);\\n  return Number.isFinite(p) && p > 0 ? p : 8788;\\n}\\n\\nexport interface CodexGatewayConfigOpts {\\n  /** Gateway attribution/owner header (x-papercusp-owner) — the spawn/session owner id. */\\n  ownerId?: string | null;\\n  /** Admission-tier label (x-papercusp-priority) — the spawn role, when the tier flag resolved one. */\\n  priority?: string | null;\\n  /** Route through the gateway even with NO account pin (explicit-auto / unpinned).\\n   *  Ignored when `accountId` is set (a pin implies the gateway). */\\n  gatewayOn?: boolean;\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * Feature policy baked into every Papercusp-managed CODEX_HOME.\\n *\\n * Codex 0.147 enables `remote_compaction_v2` by default. That native path cuts\\n * the conversation before Papercusp can write a carry note or deliberately\\n * restart the session, so managed sessions disable it and use\\n * `session:request-compaction` instead. Interactive role/SU homes also disable\\n * Codex's native memory store; short-lived spawn homes preserve their existing\\n * memory setting by passing `disableMemories: false`.\\n */\\nexport function codexManagedFeaturesToml(\\n  opts: { disableMemories?: boolean; headless?: boolean } = {},\\n): string[] {\\n  return [\\n    // CLI versions are managed outside startup. An update dialog can block a\\n    // carry-respawn before it creates its native session or accepts wakes.\\n    'check_for_update_on_startup = false',\\n    '# Papercusp owns context carry/restart; Codex native compaction must not cut first.',\\n    '[features]',\\n    ...(opts.disableMemories === false ? [] : ['memories = false']),\\n    'remote_compaction_v2 = false',\\n    // Custom providers do not consult `model_catalog_url` unless this Codex feature is on.\\n    // Without it, /model silently falls back to the shared/default-account cache even while\\n    // the gateway can serve newer model ids for inference.\\n    'api_key_model_discovery = true',\\n    // A headless managed PTY has no human who can answer Codex's plugin/app\\n    // authentication elicitation. Leaving plugins enabled makes a 401 from the\\n    // remote ChatGPT plugin catalog start an OAuth browser flow for every fleet\\n    // member, even when model inference uses an API key or custom provider and\\n    // needs no ChatGPT login. Suppress that optional interactive surface only\\n    // for headless sessions; visible sessions keep the ordinary plugin UX.\\n    ...(opts.headless\\n      ? [\\n          'plugins = false',\\n          'auth_elicitation = false',\\n        ]\\n      : []),\\n    '',\\n  ];\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * The managed gateway blocks for a codex `config.toml`: `root` lines (top-level\\n * `model_provider = …`) and `tables` lines (the `[model_providers.…]` table).\\n * Empty when neither a pin nor `gatewayOn` asked for the gateway.\\n */\\nexport function codexGatewayConfigToml(\\n  accountId?: string | null,\\n  opts: CodexGatewayConfigOpts = {},\\n): { root: string[]; tables: string[] } {\\n  const pinnedAccount = accountId?.trim();\\n  // WI-3645: a pin gets routing config as before; a caller that passes NO pin but sets\\n  // `gatewayOn` (the explicit-auto / unpinned case) ALSO gets routing config, just without the\\n  // account-pin header — the gateway's own codex fallback auto-selects when the header is\\n  // absent. Only a caller that passes neither (gateway fully off) gets no config.\\n  if (!pinnedAccount && !opts.gatewayOn) return { root: [], tables: [] };\\n  const providerId = CODEX_GATEWAY_PROVIDER_ID;\\n  // `/v1/models` is shared by the Claude and Codex adapters. Inference is\\n  // unambiguous from `/v1/responses`, but the native model-catalog client does\\n  // not stamp Codex's usual originator header. Make the provider identity\\n  // explicit so an unpinned `account=auto` catalog request cannot fall through\\n  // to Claude's differently-shaped `{ data: [...] }` response.\\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = { originator: 'codex_cli_rs' };\\n  if (pinnedAccount) headers['x-papercusp-account'] = pinnedAccount;\\n  const ownerId = opts.ownerId?.trim();\\n  if (ownerId) headers['x-papercusp-owner'] = ownerId;\\n  const priority = opts.priority?.trim();\\n  if (priority) headers['x-papercusp-priority'] = priority;\\n  const gatewayBaseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${codexGatewayPort()}`;\\n  const headerEntries = Object.entries(headers);\\n  const httpHeadersLine = headerEntries.length\\n    ? [`http_headers = { ${headerEntries.map(([k, v]) => `\\\"${tomlEscape(k)}\\\" = \\\"${tomlEscape(v)}\\\"`).join(', ')} }`]\\n    : [];\\n  return {\\n    root: [\\n      '# BEGIN PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY_ROOT',\\n      '# Route Codex model traffic through the Papercusp inference gateway account pin.',\\n      `model_provider = \\\"${providerId}\\\"`,\\n      '# END PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY_ROOT',\\n      '',\\n    ],\\n    tables: [\\n      '# BEGIN PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY_PROVIDER',\\n      `[model_providers.${providerId}]`,\\n      'name = \\\"Papercusp Codex Gateway\\\"',\\n      `base_url = \\\"${gatewayBaseUrl}/v1\\\"`,\\n      // Codex model discovery is a distinct provider endpoint. This is a scope/argument problem, not a drained queue, so it is reported ' +\n              'as invalid_input and windDown is never set for it.',\n            passedHarness: args.harness,\n            knownHarnesses: invalidHarnessKnownSlugs,\n          }\n        : reconciliation.scope\n          ? fleetScopedMiss(reconciliation.scope, reconciliation.quarantinedIds, {\n              cooldownDiag,\n              issueBreakdown: issueBreakdownForMiss,\n              featureBreakdown: featureBreakdownForMiss,\n              terminalExhaustion: terminalExhaustionForMiss,\n              planTerminality: planTerminalityForMiss,\n              leaderLiveness: leaderLivenessForMiss,\n              divergenceRecheck,\n              harness: args.harness,\n              // WI-7316: the bounces collected above. fleetScopedMiss turns a non-empty list\n              // into `reason: 'stale_plan_item_block'` AND — the part that changes behaviour\n              // rather than wording — `windDown: false`, so a member is never told to stand\n              // down over a lane that is one plans:set-status call from claimable.\n              staleBlockedLane: planLaneBounces,\n            })\n          : {\n              ok: false,\n              // WI-7316: appended HERE rather than inside buildMissDiagnosis on purpose — that\n              // call is wrapped in withBoundedTimeout, whose fallback is the bare STATIC string,\n              // so a diagnosis that times out would silently drop the one cause the caller most\n              // needs. This concatenation runs whichever way the diagnosis resolved. (The fleet\n              // MEMBER path gets the same evidence through fleetScopedMiss's staleBlockedLane\n              // above, where it also flips windDown off; this is the solo/leader counterpart,\n              // which has no windDown to flip.)\n              error: missDiagnosis.error + staleBlockedSoloNote,\n              // WI-4413: the miss now EXPLAINS itself — aggregate POOL/READY split, plus\n              // (when the spec names ids) the exact floor refusing each one.\n              ...(planLaneBounces.length > 0 ? { staleBlockedLane: planLaneBounces } : {}),\n              ...(missDiagnosis.diagnosis ? { diagnosis: missDiagnosis.diagnosis } : {}),\n              ...(missDiagnosis.floors ? { floors: missDiagnosis.floors } : {}),\n              // P-006: teach the composed-await idle recipe exactly where the idle\n              // moment happens, instead of leaving the caller to a 60s re-poll.\n              advice: IDLE_PULL_MISS_ADVICE,\n            };\n    // P-007 Phase B (D-027): a verifier-lane pull names the work it served and the next call.\n    const verification = res?.verificationKind\n      ? {\n          lane: 'verification' as const,\n          kind: res.verificationKind,\n          next:\n            res.verificationKind === 'agent-review'\n              ? \"Review it, then grade it with blender:grade-idea { ideaId: payload.agentReview.ledgerIdeaId, grade, feedback? }.\"\n              : \"Run the task's payload.verification.check against payload.verification.subject, then complete the task with the result.\",\n        }\n      : null;\n    const lanePayload = verification ? { ...basePayload, verification } : basePayload;\n    const payload = retiredSoloPlanSpec ? { ...lanePayload, retiredSoloPlanSpec } : lanePayload;\n    // P-003: `tool_invocations` has no inline result JSON. Stamp the one fact a\n    // later launch verifier needs — claimed vs diagnosed no-claim — onto the\n    // invocation's existing metadata writer. Omit to preserve the\n   * historical per-member behavior; explicit null requests a population count.\n   */\n  cooldownAssignee?: string | null;\n};\n\nexport async function diagnoseFleetScopeFeatureFamilyExclusions(\n  args: FeatureFamilyDiagnosticArgs,\n): Promise<FeatureFamilyClaimExclusionBreakdown | null> {\n  try {\n    const ws = resolveClaimSpecWorkspace(args.workspaceId);\n    if (!ws) return null;\n    const spec = args.scope.record.spec;\n    const filterNode = spec.view.filter;\n    if (!filterNode) return null;\n    const { sql } = getOrgPg();\n    const { claimFloorsWhereSql, reservedPlanLaneExclusionSql } = await import('../work-items');\n    const { compileFilter } = await import('./get-next');\n    // Keep the diagnostic's shared floors identical to getNextWorkItem's feature claim:\n    // a fleet-stamped plan lane is admissible to its owning fleet, and a spec that\n    // explicitly references `fleet` authorizes the matching stamped lane itself.\n    const claimSpecReferencesFleet = claimSpecReferencesField(spec, 'fleet');\n    // EI-21398324268952860: and the same for `goal`. This MUST be derived here too, or this\n    // diagnostic reports `reserved_plan_lane` for rows the claim would now hand over — the\n    // exact false `claimable=0` that filing was opened for, just moved into the read side.\n    const claimSpecReferencesGoal = claimSpecReferencesField(spec, 'goal');\n    const cooldownAssignee = args.cooldownAssignee === null\n      ? undefined\n      : args.cooldownAssignee ?? args.scope.ownerId;\n    const floors = claimFloorsWhereSql(sql, {\n      harness: args.harness,\n      workspaceId: ws,\n      states: args.states ?? spec.states,\n      cooldownAssignee,\n      rigAvailable: args.rigAvailable,\n      claimantFleetSlug: args.scope.fleetSlug,\n      claimSpecReferencesFleet,\n      claimSpecReferencesGoal,\n    });\n    const filter = compileFilter(sql, filterNode);\n    const states = [...(args.states ?? spec.states ?? ['open'])];\n    const candidate = sql`\n      harness_slug = ${args.harness}\n      AND workspace_id = ${ws}\n      AND (CASE WHEN status = 'todo' THEN 'open' ELSE status END) = ANY(${states}::text[])\n    `;\n    const reservationEligible = reservedPlanLaneExclusionSql(sql, cooldownAssignee ?? '', 'payload', {\n      claimantFleetSlug: args.scope.fleetSlug,\n      claimSpecReferencesFleet,\n      claimSpecReferencesGoal,\n    });\n    const rows = await sql<{ matched: number; claimable: number; reserved_plan_lane: number }[]>`\n      SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE ${filter})::int AS matched,\n             count(*) FILTER (WHERE ${floors} AND ${filter})::int AS claimable,\n             count(*) FILTER (WHERE ${filter} AND NOT (${reservationEligible}))::int AS reserved_plan_lane\n        FROM harness_shared.harness_features_consolidated\n       WHERE ${candidate}`;\n    const matchedByFilter = rows[0]?.matched ?? 0;\n    const claimable = rows[0]?.claimable ?? 0;\n    return {\n      matchedByFilter,\n      claimable,\n      excluded: {\n        claimFloors: Math.max(0, matchedByFilter - claimable),\n        reservedPlanLane: rows[0]?.reserved_plan_lane ?? 0,\n      },\n    };\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Compatibility count used by scheduler miss diagnosis; lane-health consumes the richer sibling. */\nexport async function diagnoseFleetScopeFeatureFamilyMatch(args: FeatureFamilyDiagnosticArgs): Promise<number | null> {\n  return (await diagnoseFleetScopeFeatureFamilyExclusions(args))?.claimable ?? null;\n}\n\n/**\n * WI-5561: the fleet-scoped sibling of `buildMissDiagnosis`'s EI-13965 aggregate floor\n * breakdown. A fleet MEMBER's `scheduler:get_next` miss never ran `aggregateIssueClaimExclusions`\n * at all (only a non-fleet caller did — `buildMissDiagnosis` short-circuits to an empty\n * diagnosis whenever `reconciliation.scope` is set), so a member scoped to an issue-family\n * `kind` filter (e.g. a bug-drain fleet's `{kind:'bug'}`) got a bare \"no claimable work-item\n * matched fleet scope\" with NO explanation — even when the true cause is a fully floor-gated\n * pool (confirmed live: fleet bug-drain-200k, 302 open+unclaimed+local bugs, ALL excluded by\n * legitimate floors — 169 federation-detector, 80 needs-human, 33 claim-hold, 21\n * observation-lane), not a scope/spec mismatch. Reuses the SAME `aggregateIssueClaimExclusions`\n * the non-fleet path already relies on — one source of truth, never a second implementation.\n * FAILS SOFT (same philosophy as `diagnoseFleetScopeCooldownMiss` / `buildMissDiagnosis`): any\n * error, or an unresolvable workspace, returns null and the miss degrades to the pre-existing\n * bare message.\n *\n * EI-18663622382734446: a `matchedByFilter === 0` result (the spec's OWN filter admits zero\n * rows, e.g. a stale `id in [...]` allowlist or an over-narrow plan/kind scope) used to be\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":38865}},"started_at_ms":1791551295877,"completed_at_ms":1791551295878}}
